records.speaker: Speakerless panel
records.source_meaning: The speakerless cheer is the crew's answer to the end of the speech.
records.editorial_finding: The crew answers his appeal with a cheer. The speakerless shout lets the next action speak for itself.

records.Japanese: パチパチパチパチパチ！！
records.speaker: Speakerless panel
records.source_meaning: The speakerless applause follows the cheer. The short action label suits the established staged panel.
records.editorial_finding: The applause closes the formal speech and bridges into the officers' more personal reactions.

records.Japanese:
いつもながら
提督の演説にはしびれますねえ
records.current_English: Your speeches always give me chills.
records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.previous_English: Your speeches always give me chills.
records.english: Your speeches always give me chills.
records.source_meaning: Manuel compliments Hodram's speech as something that always moves him. The plain phrase sounds spontaneous.
records.editorial_finding: Manuel says the admiral's speeches still give him chills. His direct praise suits the suddenly personal exchange.

records.Japanese:
我々がこの国に骨をうずめる気になった
のも、提督のあの熱弁にすっかり
魅せられたからだと言っても過言では
ありませんからな
records.current_English:
It's no exaggeration to say
 a speech like that is what made us 
 want to spend the rest of our lives
 in this country.
records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.previous_English: It's no exaggeration to say a speech like that is what made us want to spend the rest of our lives in this country.
records.english: It's no exaggeration to say a speech like that is what made us want to spend the rest of our lives in this country.
records.source_meaning: Gerhard recalls that the force of Hodram's oratory helped persuade them to make their lives in the country.
records.editorial_finding: Gerhard gives a fuller reason for the officers' devotion. The existing restraint and emphasis on staying in this country suit his formal voice.

records.Japanese:
そう言えば、私が武者震いってやつを
生まれて初めて知ったのも
FA提督の
訓示でしたよ
records.current_English:
One of your speeches,
 Admiral FA, 
 was the first thing that ever made 
 me shake with eagerness for battle.
records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.previous_English: One of your speeches, Admiral FA, was the first thing that ever made me shake with eagerness for battle.
records.english: One of your speeches, Admiral FA, was the first thing that ever made me shake with eagerness for battle.
records.source_meaning: Charles recalls a strong physical excitement at the prospect of battle. Keep the captain's surname substitution.
records.editorial_finding: Charles names the admiral by surname and remembers his first physical thrill before battle. Keep the original address and single FA placement. The latest ordinary replay confirms the four-line display.

records.Japanese:
…よさないか
あれは俺が最も苦痛としている責務の
ひとつだ。それより…
records.current_English:
Enough of that. Few duties 
 are as painful 
 as giving a speech. Anyway...
records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.previous_English: Enough of that. Few duties are as painful as giving a speech. Anyway...
records.english: Enough of that. Few duties are as painful as giving a speech. Anyway...
records.source_meaning: Hodram is uncomfortable with the praise and pivots from his most painful duties to business.
records.editorial_finding: Hodram brushes off the compliments and admits that public speaking is one of his most painful duties. The English carries that dry shift. Keep the comparison together and reserve the brief Anyway for his deliberate pivot to policy.
proposed_visual_lines: are as painful as giving a speech.
records.intentional_final_pause: The last word marks the topic shift from the crew’s praise to state policy.

records.Japanese:
これからは敵対国の艦隊や海賊を
撃破すれば、その戦果に応じて国から
報償金が出ることになったそうだ
records.current_English:
Word is, the state will pay us for 
 defeating enemy fleets and pirates.
 How much we get
 depends on what we accomplish.
records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.previous_English: Word is, the state will pay us for defeating enemy fleets and pirates. How much we get depends on what we accomplish.
records.english: Word is, the state will pay us for defeating enemy fleets and pirates. The reward depends on our results.
records.source_meaning: The new policy pays state rewards according to results. Hodram reports what he has been told.
records.editorial_finding: Hodram relays the newly established state reward. State payment, qualifying enemy fleets or pirates, and rewards based on results all stay explicit. The final sentence names the reward directly and reads as a single spoken thought.
protected_phrases: The reward depends on our results.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.source_meaning: Manuel's quick exclamation suits his excitement at the prospect of rewards.
records.editorial_finding: Manuel responds in one enthusiastic beat. The uncomplicated exclamation suits his reaction.

records.Japanese:
艦隊の予算を拡充する環境が
整ったというわけですね
records.current_English:
So now we'll have a way to raise 
 more money for the fleet.
records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.previous_English: So now we'll have a way to raise more money for the fleet.
records.english: So now we'll have a way to raise more money for the fleet.
records.source_meaning: Charles draws the practical conclusion about increasing fleet funds.
records.editorial_finding: Charles connects the new payment directly to funding the fleet. The inference follows naturally from Hodram's report.

records.Japanese: いよいよ攻勢に出られますな
records.current_English: At last, we can go on the offensive.
records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.previous_English: At last, we can go on the offensive.
records.english: At last, we can go on the offensive.
records.source_meaning: Gerhard sees the change as a chance to take the initiative rather than a command to attack immediately.
records.editorial_finding: Gerhard takes the new policy as a chance to go on the offensive. The existing line keeps his satisfaction and avoids turning it into an immediate order.

records.Japanese:
ハンザ同盟の船が、無断で我々の領海を
侵犯しているという、例の報告を早く
確かめねばならん。どうやら、今日の
獲物はアテがはずれたようだ
records.current_English:
Check that report
 of Hanseatic ships trespassing 
 in our waters. It seems we went
 after the wrong quarry today.
records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.previous_English: Check that report of Hanseatic ships trespassing in our waters. It seems we went after the wrong quarry today.
records.english: We need to check that report soon. Hanseatic ships may be trespassing in our waters. Looks like we went after the wrong quarry today.
records.source_meaning: Hodram wants the unauthorized incursion report checked promptly. His assessment of their earlier quarry remains tentative.
records.editorial_finding: Hodram changes the subject from the opportunity to the urgent report. The Japanese says the crew must check it soon and only tentatively concludes they picked the wrong quarry today. Keep both degrees of uncertainty and the Hanseatic incursion.

records.Japanese:
船員たちに一休みさせたら
すぐにでも出港準備をしておけ
records.current_English:
Give the crew a short rest, then 
 get us ready to sail right away.
records.speaker: Hodram Bergstrom
records.previous_English: Give the crew a short rest, then get us ready to sail right away.
records.english: Give the crew a short rest, then get us ready to sail right away.
records.source_meaning: The rest comes before immediate preparation to leave.
records.editorial_finding: He orders a short rest before immediate preparations to depart. The existing ordering and steady register work.

records.speaker: Gerhard Adernkatz
records.source_meaning: Gerhard's formal assent fits his established manner and the closing trio of replies.
records.editorial_finding: Gerhard gives a clipped formal acknowledgment.

records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.source_meaning: Charles's nautical acknowledgment stands between Gerhard's and Manuel's.
records.editorial_finding: Charles acknowledges the order with a nautical Aye. The source uses a different acknowledgment from Gerhard's.

records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.source_meaning: Manuel ends on the distinctive two-part nautical acknowledgment.
records.editorial_finding: Manuel closes the exchange with a distinctive Aye, aye, corresponding to the Japanese loan expression.
